distinguishing_features: Prevents fillet fatigue crack initiation by shifting the crankshaft's first natural frequency away from the firing frequency band
Modifies inertia distribution and bearing stiffness of the crankshaft rather than detecting or inferring damage
Changes the cyclic stress range Δσ at the fillet via resonance decoupling without altering fillet geometry or Kt
Design-time FEA pass/fail criterion f_n,new > 1.15 × f_firing,max with no new sensors or monitoring hardware
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to reduce the cyclic stress amplitude driving fillet fatigue crack initiation in an existing crankshaft design without relying on local fillet geometry changes or added damping/monitoring hardware.
parsed.viable_reason: The mechanism is internally inconsistent and physically implausible: adding mass (relief pockets) to the free end lowers rather than raises the natural frequency, the discrete k/I formula conflates torsional and bending modes, and a +20% shift of a ~100 Hz mode via passive inertia bearing-stiffness tweaks is not achievable at the stated scale while also stiffening 'bearing clearances'.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Frequency tuning via inertia/stiffness redistribution is a recognized design step, but none of the prior art is in this domain or addresses resonance avoidance of crankshaft natural modes, so the specific distinguishing mechanism is not an obvious application of the cited art.
